title: Audit Harvest Proxy for Residency Verification and Retention Manifests
creator: Maya Chen
description: Scope: Build a lightweight, extensible 'Audit Harvest Proxy' service that sits alongside the control evidence collectors and normalizes residency and retention metadata into signed artifacts (manifests) consumable by the Compliance Console and downstream auditors. The proxy should: 1) gather region/zone and retention-policy metadata from multiple sources (runtime routing, storage connectors, DB export jobs, Dedicated deployment configs); 2) reconcile policy-to-artifact mappings (SOC 2 control IDs, ISO 27001 statements); 3) emit compact, verifiable manifests with provenance headers and optional signed snapshots for long-term retention. Goal is to automate 70%+ of evidence correlation for region-bound controls and to support both Hosted and Private deployments with minimal configuration.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy collects residency metadata from at least three sources (request routing, storage indexer, deployment config) and normalizes into a single artifact format
Artifacts include a manifest schema with fields: control_mapping, source_refs, retention_policy_id, timestamp, signer_id, and content_hash
Generated manifests are accepted by the Compliance Console ingest API and appear on the per-customer evidence timeline
Proof artifacts can be rotated and re-signed by integration with KMS (for Hosted) and HSM/KMS config hooks for Private deployments
End-to-end test covering mismatch scenarios (e.g., declared residency vs actual storage location) with alerting and automated remediation suggestions
tasks: Design manifest schema and provenance header (schema draft: confluence link)
Implement lightweight HTTP proxy with adapters for storage indexer, runtime-router, and deployment-config service
Add a reconciliation engine to detect residency/retention mismatches and tag artifacts with confidence scores
Integrate signing flow: Hosted -> KMS; Private -> customer-provided KMS/HSM reference
Create Compliance Console ingest endpoint contract and update ingest docs
Build e2e test harness with synthetic workloads and a small on-prem emulator
progress_updates: 2026-02-12 - Maya Chen: Initial scoping session with PM and Compliance. Decided to prioritize manifest schema compatibility with existing audit exports.
2026-02-18 - Rafael Ortega: PoC proxy implemented (node) that pulls storage location from the indexer and emits a JSON manifest. Added basic provenance header.
2026-02-25 - Security review kickoff: pointed out requirement to support customer-provided KMS keys in Private mode. Added to backlog as mandatory for GA.
2026-03-04 - Rafael Ortega: Reconciliation engine prototype returns confidence scores. Found edge case when objects are moved between regions; creating a follow-up task to surface object move events.
2026-03-10 - PM review: Product wants a signed digest that matches what the external auditor can verify without Redwood Console access. Adding external-verifier README.
decisions: Use a compact JSON-LD-like manifest (v1) with a small set of required headers to keep storage cost low
Sign manifests with KMS-backed signing keys; expose verification endpoint for auditors where appropriate
Keep proxy language-agnostic: core adapters will be implemented in Go for performance, web hooks and tests may use Node.js
Do not attempt to enforce retention in-host at GA for Private deployments; instead provide detection, alerts, and remediation guidance to ops teams
Expose confidence scoring in the artifact to enable Console rule filters (auto-triage mismatches)
risks_mitigation: Risk: mismapped residency due to lag in storage indexer. Mitigation: include 'observed_at' timestamps and last-known-location history in artifacts
Risk: signing key management complexity for Private customers. Mitigation: documented KMS-HSM onboarding flow and a verification-only mode that accepts customer-provided public keys
Risk: large volume of manifests causing cost/ingest pressure. Mitigation: configurable sampling window and delta-only manifests for high-volume customers
test_plan: Unit tests for each adapter and manifest serializer
Integration tests: proxy -> indexer -> console ingest using a test tenant
Chaos test: simulate object move events and verify artifacts contain history and confidence changes
Performance test: sustained 500 manifests/min ingest for a medium-sized tenant with delta manifests enabled
follow_up: Add a UI in Compliance Console to view artifact provenance and confidence score
Pilot with two enterprise customers (one Hosted, one Private) for 30 days
Post-mortem and cost analysis after pilot to tune sampling and retention defaults
